Scrape out old putty to bare wood. If pane is intact, you can remove for more thorough cleaning. Any shit on glass is easy to remove: take a new straight edge razor and slide it along glass surface, lifting off any residue. Mind not to roll the blade over and slice your fingers holding the blade - use short strokes for better stability.

Once old glaze is off, replace pane and hold in place using push tabs (little metal tabs about 1/4" with a pointed side you shove into frame against glass pane). Buy you some "glazier putty". Take a dollop with 1" knife and work it on a non-porous surface (can use inside of lid) to smooth out consistency. Take small amounts on tip of knife and apply along pane, scraping off away from pane. When you've enough built up on a side, take the square end of knife and run it along at about 35 deg. I'd do all 4 sides, then you take the side of a fingertip and run it down the putty, creating a running slightly concave surface. Do all 4 sides. Take a damp shop paper towel and clean off excess from frame and glass. The take your straight edge razor and make a clean edge of putty on the glass: with edge parallel with edge of pane, with blade edge facing putty at about 45 deg, bring blade down onto glass and quickly pull razor towards center of pane, creating a crisp line along the putty (easier demonstrated than written).

Putty will be hard in a day. Can paint.

Tip: the razor can be used to clean any glass/mirror. I use SprayWay brand cleaner (I still keep spray cans in truck, even though it's been yrs) wipe with no-lint shop paper towel (those blue ones) and use razor to slice off any crud.
